item.title: The European AI literacy framework expected in December arrived in June, with the PISA 2029 assessment in the background
item.description: In November 2025, anyone looking for ways to teach critical thinking with artificial intelligence was pointed to a framework still in draft, with the final version announced for December. It arrived six months later.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”: a text document, “Draft”, and below it an empty dotted box. On the right, labelled “Today”: the same document, now with a check mark, “Version 1.0”, and below it a filled box that reads “PISA 2029”.

item.title: GPT-5.1 arrived in ChatGPT to amazement at its speed and did not last four months there
item.description: In November 2025, people were struck by how quickly GPT-5.1, OpenAI’s “more conversational” model, arrived. By 11 March 2026 it had already disappeared from ChatGPT.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, a chat bubble with lines of text and the label “GPT-5.1”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same bubble but dashed and in blue, with the label “GPT-5.1” struck through and “Retired” below.

item.title: Gemini’s formulas reached Google Docs as code; a year on, Docs still does not understand LaTeX
item.description: In November 2025, Gemini was already writing and editing formulas in LaTeX, but when they were taken into Google Docs they arrived as code. A year on, Google’s word processor still cannot read LaTeX and the remedy is the same: an add-on or a separate editor.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a Google Docs page with the formula turned into code braces, labelled “Code”. On the right, “Today”: the same page with the same “Code”, and a blue arrow pointing to a blue puzzle piece labelled “Add-on”, the remedy that is still needed.

item.title: The open model that was “checkmating” the giants: a year on, Kimi is almost three times bigger and still behind
item.description: In November 2025, people were sharing that a Chinese open-weights model, Kimi K2 Thinking, beat GPT-5 on some tests. Today Kimi K3, from the same family, is almost three times bigger, but its maker admits it does not match the best closed models.

item.title: A word cloud with a “backend” in a single prompt: today Claude’s new artifacts save data without being published
item.description: In November 2025, a word cloud built with Claude stored everyone’s votes from a single prompt. Today the new artifacts save data without needing to be published.

media:content.media:description: A word cloud with a “backend” in a single prompt: today Claude’s new artifacts save data without being published

item.title: From the character who warped within eight seconds to models that keep them the same from scene to scene
item.description: In November 2025, animating a character with Veo 3 meant cutting the clip before it stopped looking like itself. Today Google promises to keep it consistent from scene to scene.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: an “8 s” bar with one character at the start and, after the cut, another drawn warped and in dashes. On the right, “Today”: a longer “15 s” bar with the same character repeated three times, identical, in blue.

item.title: NotebookLM presentations, once impossible to tweak, can now be revised slide by slide
item.description: A year ago, anyone wanting an editable presentation had to leave NotebookLM. Today the tool, which no longer even goes by that name, makes slides, amends them on request and exports them to PowerPoint.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a slide with a play triangle and a padlock, labelled “Video locked”. On the right, “Today”: the same slide, in blue, with lines of text and a pencil, labelled “Editable”.
